- Expected heads in flips 6 and 7: about 1.12
- Public fair value: about 4.12

The settlement S = 3 + X, where X is the number of heads in flips 6 and 7, has these approximate probabilities: S=3 at 0.21, S=4 at 0.46, S=5 at 0.33.

Only the bid is allowed. Buying at bid b earns S − b per unit. Two groups can trade with me:

- **Noise sellers** (prob 0.8) sell when their valuation, distributed N(4.12, 2.7), is below b. Their trades carry no adverse selection, so the expected profit per trade is 4.12 − b.

Expected profit is roughly 0.8 · Φ((b − 4.12)/2.7) · (4.12 − b). This peaks near b ≈ 1.9, at about 0.37 per quote. A bid of 1.9 also reduces my short position from −3 toward −2, and it sits well below the informed-seller threshold.

**Ask:** Informed buyers only buy when S > ask. Since S ≤ 6, an ask at or above 6 never meets an informed buyer. The noise buyers have valuation ~ N(5.94, 2.6). Maximising (ask − 5.94) × P(valuation > ask) gives a standardised cutoff z ≈ 0.75, so ask ≈ 5.94 + 0.75 × 2.6 ≈ 7.9.

**Bid:** Informed sellers only sell when S < bid. A bid of 3.9 is below every possible S, so none arrive. Applying the same logic on the other side, the optimal bid is about 5.94 − 0.75 × 2.6 ≈ 3.9.

Both prices are chosen to avoid informed counterparties, so the expected profit from each side is positive: about 1.9 per noise sale at 7.9 and about 1.9 per noise purchase at 3.9, weighted by their trade probabilities.
